request: Explain barely visible nozzle glow and expose exhaust temperature in the Engine tab.

implementation.home: Engine → Temperatures and oil → EGT (exhaust gas)
implementation.behavior: Shows catalog-present native read-only Celsius EGT; updates through cooling; nonfinite reads show n/a. Legacy Fahrenheit remains optional. Tooltip distinguishes modeled gas from nozzle-metal and afterburner-exit measurements.
implementation.unchanged: No optical table, native temperature equation, material selection, geometry, brightness gain, orb/summary or phone behavior changed in this follow-up.

audit.interpretation: The chosen upper-reference display normalization makes ordinary modeled full-power heat much dimmer. The pipeline follows the specified lookup, but this does not establish realistic F135 appearance.
audit.geometry: Exact and neighboring nozzle-axis rays hit the opaque double-sided darkmet2 center cap first. The existing glow material includes that cap. Vertex radii alone would have missed the spanning cap triangles.
limits: Native EGT is generic modeled gas temperature, not measured F135 hardware temperature.
The .25 display reference is arbitrary; material emissivity and gas-to-metal relationship are not calibrated.
The scene uses uncalibrated hemispheric lighting/exposure, so relative Planck radiance alone cannot establish on-screen physical brightness.
No new GPU run or pixel measurement; numerical brightness estimates are not rendered-image qualification.

primarySources.supports: Emissive color and physical light-to-pixel interpretation depend on camera exposure.
Blackbody spectral-radiance calibration and Planck law.
